findings.title: A filter driver with a non-UTF-8 name still runs a program during snapshot and compare
A malformed snapshot file can pass compare, crash it with unexpected <Type>, or give a false violation
An ignored file's deletion is hidden when the run pushes the ignored count over 20000
An unreadable untracked directory is skipped silently and edits inside it pass the integrity check
snapshot hangs forever when a file is swapped for a fifo between lstat and open
Run against a linked worktree, the check misses a branch switch in the main worktree
Every snapshot reads the whole Git LFS object store, gigabytes per run on LFS-heavy repos
In ignored-overflow mode, removing a nested ignored directory is not reported
A config include pointing at a fifo hangs snapshot because git calls have no timeout
Changes under .git/worktrees/<name>/ other than HEAD (index, config.worktree, refs, lock) are not reported
Many files just under 64 MiB are each read in full; sampling bounds cost per file, not per snapshot
The git-dir walk makes 3x the islink and 5x the lstat calls of 0.3.1 on rr-cache-style trees
On macOS a file more than 1000 directories deep is invisible to the snapshot despite the changelog claim
The unreadable git-dir file error names a path that looks like a work-tree path
The snapshot format break is not labelled breaking and the version is still 0.3.1
compare --allow costs paths times allow entries
Above-cap ignored trees and loose objects still cost linear work that the snapshot throws away
The PRD allocator creates a backlog directory outside the repo when prds is swapped for a symlink mid-run
